steps.body: Four addends are just one more stage: pair, bank, join, join. The running total carries you the whole way.
steps.narration: Four addends are just one more stage: pair, bank, join, join. The running total carries you the whole way.

widget.prompt: Four addends staged: the total reached 55; the last addend is 10. Hop it.

commonLandings.feedback: A one-hop — this final addend is worth a full ten.

widget.missFeedback: Each hop adds 10. From 55, 1 hops land on 65.
widget.successFeedback: Landed on 65 — four addends, three joins, one steady total.

predict.prompt: Adding four numbers needs how many joins?
predict.reveal: Each join folds in one more addend: pair (1), third (2), fourth (3).

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2n four addends.
invariants: Regrouping addends changes the ORDER of joining, never the total — every staging of the sum must land on the same number for g2n four addends.
misconceptions: Believing the grouping or order of addends can change a sum, or letting an addend join twice or not at all while restaging.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: Which single change to the staging would actually change the total — and which only changes the path?

explanationVariants: The third addend joins the pair's total.

commonErrors.feedback: That skipped ahead to 9 — the addends join in the order you staged.
The total froze; 11 must be folded in before moving on.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Stage the sum: pick a pair, bank the total, and let each remaining addend join one at a time.

hints: Pick a pair and add it.

widget.prompt: You add 34 + 19 + 6 + 1 as (19 + 1) + (34 + 6). Can the new grouping change the total?

options.label: No — the same addends make the same total
options.feedback: Correct — (19 + 1) + (34 + 6) is 20 + 40 = 60, exactly where the left-to-right path lands.

options.label: Yes — pairing changed the addends
options.feedback: The addends are untouched — 34, 19, 6, and 1 each still join exactly once; only the order moved.

options.label: Only if each pair makes a ten
options.feedback: Friendly pairs make the adding easier, but the freedom to regroup works for every pair, ten or not.

options.label: Yes — four addends is too many to regroup
options.feedback: The rule has no addend limit — with four addends you may even regroup twice, as both pairs show.

hints: Pick a pair and add it.
